content.comment_body: Hello, in my program, there's a menu with several screens designed to let users adjust parameters. Normally, this involves holding a key, selecting the parameter, confirming with enter, changing it, and then exiting. Since most screens display only a single parameter, I'm wondering if it’s possible to modify a parameter more directly with key combinations (like escape and arrows). It seems this isn't supported natively, and even attempts outside the standard blocks don't allow detection of the active screen, making it impossible to select the right parameter to change. Is there any way to access this information?

Hello [user_name], You can find an application example about menu control with [product_name] on the [company_name] homepage. Instead of using the function keys of the [product_name] operator device, you could use the cursor keys of the [product_name] base module to navigate the menu and modify values. [url] Choose 'Display' in the application example overview for easier access. Hope this helps! Best regards, [user_name]

Thank you for the examples! Sadly, my current program is nearly at its block limit, so I can’t implement this solution now, but I might consider it for smaller projects. It’s unfortunate that there isn’t a simpler built-in method for this.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are frustrated by the complexity required to adjust parameters directly within menus. Although some application examples enable navigation and changes via function or cursor keys, these approaches demand additional programming resources, which may be prohibitive when programs approach capacity limits. There is a consistent desire for easier native methods for direct parameter modification.
analysis.user_expectations: Users are looking for a streamlined, built-in solution to adjust parameters shown on-screen using simple key commands—ideally without complicated menu logic or extra programming resources.
